text:
Anya: Quick sync — draft guidance for field network cutovers for Private deployments (VPC & on-prem). Asking ops + eng for acceptance criteria before we lock roadmap slice. TL;DR: target 2 upgrade lanes (online patching for VPC, staged operator for air-gapped).
Samir: +1. Need clarity on max allowable token-serving downtime in the canary window.
Jess: Customers keep asking for <2m token latency during handoffs. Many will accept a brief control-plane flapping if data plane stays warm.
Ben: Technical reality: for on-prem airgapped installs, the operator bundle restart takes ~3–5m on older nodes. We can optimize but not guarantee <2m without faster state migration.
Anya: Noted. Proposal: define two launch gates — Gate A (VPC): 99.9% token-path SLA during cutover; Gate B (Airgap): 99.0% with documented restart window. Field teams can opt into Gate B for constrained customers.
Kai: For rollout playbook, we should include a migration checklist for customer-netops. Suggest items: BGP/preferred-eip mapping, DNS TTL changeplan, health-probe windows, egress IP preservation.
Jess: Adding team ask — include a rollback-fast-path: pin prior operator + disable new SR-rolling update. Customers want a 15m revert window.
Samir: Implementation notes: we'll add a "fast-failover" flag to the operator that toggles immediate traffic routing to fallback model variant. We need QA on KV cache invalidation.
Ben: KV cache invalidation is the tricky bit. If we failover mid-request, we could double-charge tokens or cause partial outputs. Suggest we implement request-level fencing and a small grace TTL for cached prefixes (30s) during cutover.
CustomerOps: Customer constraint: some large customers require explicit IP preservation for whitelisting — can we guarantee egress IPs for VPC Dedicated during the canary? If not, they won't sign.
Anya: For Dedicated VPC we can offer static egress via NAT gateways — requires a marketable bullet in the contract. Will add to go/no-go criteria.
NetOpsBot: Deployment template snippet for field-runbook:
```
# cutover-runbook excerpt
- precheck: verify egress-ip pinned
- dns: lower TTL to 30s
- canary: 1% traffic -> new operator for 15m
- observe: latency, token-error-rate, kv-miss-rate
- commit: gradual ramp 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 10m holds
- rollback: set operator.flag.fast_fallback = true
```
Samir: QA plan: synthetic prompt set (500 prompts) + perf harness; require no more than 3 regressions vs baseline and p95 latency within 10% during ramp.
Jess: Field acceptance: document checklist (customer consent, scheduled maintenance window, contact list, rollback trigger thresholds). We'll own customer comms.
Anya: Action items: Samir to spec the operator fast-fallback + KV grace TTL (due EOD Wed). Ben to prototype restart-time improvements (PR by next sprint). Kai & Jess to produce field runbook draft and template email (due Thu). I'll fold these into the roadmap ticket and flag as "launch-blocking" if not met.
Ben: One more — we should surface cost impact for customers (temporary burst capacity) in the runbook. Ops requests a cost-estimate table per tenant size.
Anya: Agreed. Add cost table to runbook. Anyone object to locking this slice next week?
Kai: No objections. :thumbsup:
CustomerOps: we'll start flagging customers who require IP-preserve in CRM so sales/RM can prioritize.
Anya: Great — thanks all. Will post PRD link once I merge the runbook draft.
